Hi Miriam,

Thanks again for the sync today — good conversation on the traffic pattern changes since the model upgrade. We dug into the telemetry and put together a practical proposal to avoid the repeated cold-starts and tail latencies you've been seeing at peak. Attached is a capacity worksheet with the assumptions (capacity_calc_skycove_v1.xlsx).

High-level recommendation (short):
- Convert 40 GPUs to a dedicated commit for Q4 (4:1 safety margin on current p95 sustained seq length), staged as 20 now / 20 in 30d.
- Reserve a 10-GPU burst pool for headroom during marketing spikes (no charge until used > 72 hours).
- Apply a 6% unit discount on the tranche if you commit 12 months; otherwise standard monthly reserved pricing applies.

Why this size:
- Your recent 30-day telemetry: sustained average equates to ~150 GPU-minutes/hour; p95 peaks imply ~320 GPU-minutes/hour. The 40-GPU commit gives ~2.5x buffer over p95 when combined with KV prefix caching and the burst pool.

Next steps:
1) Quick technical handoff with Marcus for kernel/latency expectations — 30 minutes.
2) Vanessa will draft an amendment for your procurement team with the staged delivery and billing triggers.
3) If agreeable, we can issue a provisional DocuSign pre-approval link and schedule the roll-in.

Attachments: capacity_calc_skycove_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet); draft amendment will follow.

Are you available Wednesday 10:00am PT for the handoff?

Hi all — quick technical note from the infra side to make sure expectations line up: 

Assumptions used in the worksheet and what we'll enforce on the tranche:
- Model kernel mix: 70% causal generation kernels / 30% embedding/utility ops — this matters for memory vs compute contention.
- Batch sizing: we used an average effective batch of 2.6 requests per GPU-step for the baseline; this compresses under burst but we've allowed conservative headroom.
- Quantization: INT8 profile tested (no quality drop in your eval harness) — saves ~28% memory allowing denser placement.
- KV cache eviction policy: LRU with 20k key capacity per vGPU partition.

Operational plan (staged roll-in):
- Phase 1 (Day 0-14): spin up 20 GPUs as dedicated; warm KV caches with a staged traffic ramp (10% -> 60% over 48h). Run latency/P95 checks at 24h and 72h.
- Phase 2 (Day 30): add remaining 20 GPUs and transfer commit billing start for tranche B once the 30d util trigger passes.
- Burst pool: 10 GPUs that can be attached dynamically; billed only if used >72 consecutive hours, or >200 GPU-minutes/day average over a 7-day window.

Expected outcome: p95 ~310ms (median expectation) during standard traffic. For the campaign spike profile you sent, we conservatively expect p95 to remain <360ms even pre-Phase 2 with the burst pool active.

I attached the micro-benchmark summary (runtimes_and_latency.pdf) and included a short checklist for rollout. I will coordinate a dry-run the week of Aug 6 if you want an ops rehearsal.
